content.overview: Section 110(1) provides that, notwithstanding anything contained in the Act, a company (a) shall transact by postal ballot such items of business as the Central Government may by notification declare to be transacted only by postal ballot, and (b) may transact by postal ballot any other item of business other than ordinary business and any business in respect of which directors or auditors have a right to be heard at any meeting, in the manner prescribed, instead of at a general meeting. A proviso (inserted by Act 1 of 2018) allows a company required to provide electronic voting under section 108 to transact a clause-(a) item at a general meeting in the manner provided in that section. Section 110(2) deems a resolution assented to by the requisite majority by postal ballot to have been duly passed at a general meeting convened in that behalf.
content.glance: Notified business must be transacted by postal ballot; other business (except ordinary business and business on which directors or auditors have a right to be heard) may be. A resolution passed by the requisite majority by postal ballot is deemed passed at a general meeting. Companies under section 108 may use the e-voting route for notified items under the 2018 proviso.
content.study:
## Section 110 — postal ballot

**Subsection (1): mandatory and optional postal ballot.** Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, a company—
- (a) shall, in respect of such items of business as the Central Government may, by notification, declare to be transacted only by means of postal ballot; and
- (b) may, in respect of any item of business, other than ordinary business and any business in respect of which directors or auditors have a right to be heard at any meeting, transact by means of postal ballot,
in such manner as may be prescribed, instead of transacting such business at a general meeting.

**Proviso (Act 1 of 2018, w.e.f. 9-2-2018).** Any item of business required to be transacted by means of postal ballot under clause (a) may be transacted at a general meeting by a company which is required to provide the facility to members to vote by electronic means under section 108, in the manner provided in that section.

**Subsection (2): deemed general-meeting resolution.** If a resolution is assented to by the requisite majority of the shareholders by means of postal ballot, it shall be deemed to have been duly passed at a general meeting convened in that behalf.

**What the section does not list.** The specific items that must go only by postal ballot are declared by Central Government notification (historically reflected in Rule 22(16) of the Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014). The manner of conducting a postal ballot is prescribed by rules. Do not invent the notified list as if it were written in section 110 itself.

**Boundaries.** Ordinary business and business on which directors or auditors have a right to be heard cannot be transacted by optional postal ballot under clause (b). One Person Companies and companies with members up to two hundred have historically been excluded from mandatory postal-ballot items under the rules; verify the current rule text.

## Apply the provision
- Identify whether the item is notified mandatory business (clause (a)), optional under clause (b), or excluded (ordinary business / right to be heard).
- Check whether the company is one required to provide electronic voting under section 108; if so, the 2018 proviso may allow a clause-(a) item to be done at a general meeting in the section 108 manner.
- Confirm the requisite majority and the prescribed manner before treating the resolution as deemed passed under subsection (2).

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

sections.heading: Subsection (1): mandatory and optional postal ballot
sections.body: A company shall transact notified items only by postal ballot (clause (a)), and may transact other items by postal ballot except ordinary business and business on which directors or auditors have a right to be heard (clause (b)), in the prescribed manner instead of at a general meeting.

sections.heading: Proviso: section 108 route for notified items
sections.body: A company required to provide electronic voting under section 108 may transact a clause-(a) notified item at a general meeting in the manner provided in that section.

sections.heading: Subsection (2): deemed passage
sections.body: A resolution assented to by the requisite majority by postal ballot is deemed to have been duly passed at a general meeting convened in that behalf.

examples.title: Notified item must go by postal ballot
examples.body: An item has been notified by the Central Government as business that must be transacted only by postal ballot. Under section 110(1)(a) the company must use postal ballot for that item, unless the 2018 proviso applies because the company is required to provide electronic voting under section 108. This is an educational illustration, not advice about a real resolution.

examples.title: Ordinary business cannot use optional postal ballot
examples.body: The company proposes to declare a dividend (ordinary business at an AGM). Clause (b) excludes ordinary business from optional postal ballot. The item cannot be put through section 110(1)(b). This is an educational illustration.

hypotheticals.question: A company required to provide electronic voting under section 108 has a notified clause-(a) item. Can it transact that item at a general meeting instead of by postal ballot?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes, under the proviso to section 110(1) inserted by Act 1 of 2018: any item required under clause (a) may be transacted at a general meeting by a company which is required to provide the facility to members to vote by electronic means under section 108, in the manner provided in that section. Confirm that the company falls within the section 108 class and follow the prescribed e-voting manner.

hypotheticals.question: Shareholders assent to a resolution by postal ballot with the requisite majority. Is a physical general meeting still required for the resolution to be valid?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Subsection (2) provides that if a resolution is assented to by the requisite majority of the shareholders by means of postal ballot, it shall be deemed to have been duly passed at a general meeting convened in that behalf.

distinctions.title: Section 110 compared with sections 107, 108 and 109
distinctions.left: Section 110 — postal ballot (mandatory notified items and optional other items)
distinctions.right: Section 107 — show of hands; section 108 — electronic voting; section 109 — demand for poll

rows.left: When must or may business be done by postal ballot instead of at a meeting?
rows.right: How is a resolution voted at a meeting, and when is electronic voting available?

rows.left: Postal ballot (or, under the proviso, general meeting with e-voting for notified items)
rows.right: General meeting (show of hands, poll, or electronic means under s. 108)

rows.left: Excludes ordinary business and business with a right to be heard from optional postal ballot
rows.right: Do not treat postal ballot as a substitute for every meeting resolution

misconceptions.trap: Treating ordinary business as eligible for optional postal ballot under clause (b).
misconceptions.correction: Clause (b) expressly excludes ordinary business and any business in respect of which directors or auditors have a right to be heard.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming every company must use postal ballot for notified items with no alternative.
misconceptions.correction: The 2018 proviso allows a company required to provide electronic voting under section 108 to transact a clause-(a) item at a general meeting in the section 108 manner.

misconceptions.trap: Listing specific notified items as if they were written in section 110 itself.
misconceptions.correction: Section 110(1)(a) refers to items the Central Government may by notification declare. The detailed list is in notifications/rules (e.g. Rule 22(16)); verify the current official text.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 110 provide?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Section 110 requires notified business to be transacted only by postal ballot, allows optional postal ballot for other business except ordinary business and business on which directors or auditors have a right to be heard, and deems a resolution passed by the requisite majority by postal ballot to have been passed at a general meeting. Companies under section 108 may use the e-voting route for notified items under the 2018 proviso.
